about: Homework for this pillar, one list per AI (Claude writes it; tools/kit/render.py in jpavia10/prometheus-hub turns it into docs/agents/QUEUE_{ai}.md and the Drive docs). Every task says exactly what to read, what to make, how many, where to save it, how Claude checks it and what makes it not done. tasks.title: Kairos Meridian: the yearly deadlines a California homeowner and driver actually has
tasks.why: Owner, 2026-11-16: homework that is legit (it changes what the pillar can do) and detailed enough that it cannot be done wrong.
tasks.unlocks: Kairos puts each one on the calendar with its real rule, so property tax, registration and tax dates stop being remembered by hand.
steps: List every yearly deadline from these agencies that applies to someone who owns a home in Kern County, drives a registered car and a registered motorcycle, and files California and federal income tax: Kern County Treasurer-Tax Collector (both property-tax installments, supplemental bills), California DMV (vehicle and motorcycle registration, smog check rule for a 2025 hybrid, license renewal), Franchise Tax Board and IRS (filing, extension, the four estimated-tax dates), Covered California open enrollment, voter registration deadlines.
Open the agency's own page for each and copy the rule as written; compute next_due from today.
Leave out anything that does not apply to that person; say 'not stated' rather than guess.

deliver.shape: JSON array, one object per row, exactly the fields below and nothing else

fields.name: title
fields.rule: what is due, under 60 characters, e.g. 'Property tax, first installment'

fields.name: rule
fields.rule: the date rule exactly as the agency states it, e.g. 'due Nov 1, delinquent after Dec 10 at 5 p.m.'

fields.name: next_due
fields.rule: the next date this falls on from today; if the rule moves for weekends, apply it

fields.name: repeats
fields.type: one of: yearly, every 2 years, twice a year, monthly
fields.rule: how often

fields.name: applies_if
fields.rule: who it applies to, e.g. 'owns a home in Kern County', 'has a registered vehicle'

fields.name: penalty
fields.rule: the penalty in the agency's words, or 'not stated'

fields.name: agency
fields.rule: the agency's name

fields.name: url
fields.rule: the exact page that shows this row, opened by you today; never a home page or search page

fields.name: quote
fields.rule: the sentence on that page that proves the row, copied word for word (under 300 characters)

fields.name: as_of
fields.rule: the date you read the page

example.title: Property tax, first installment
example.rule: Due November 1; delinquent after 5 p.m. December 10
example.applies_if: owns real property in Kern County
example.penalty: 10% penalty if not paid by the delinquency date

tasks.why: Kairos imports and exports recurring events (RRULE) but has no test that its recurrences land on the right days. RFC 5545 section 3.8.5.3 lists about 40 worked examples with their answers: turned into data, they are the test.
tasks.unlocks: A Kairos proof that runs every RFC example through its recurrence code, so a recurring bill or custody day is never off by one.
steps: Take every example in RFC 5545 section 3.8.5.3 in order (they start 'Daily for 10 occurrences').

For each: the RFC's description line, its DTSTART line, its RRULE line (and RDATE/EXDATE if the example has them), and the occurrences the RFC lists after '==>', written out as full ISO local datetimes in America/New_York (e.g. 1997-09-02T09:00). Where the RFC lists more than 20 or the rule is unbounded, give the first 20 and set truncated true.
Do not compute occurrences the RFC does not list; copy its own answers. Where the RFC's answer shows a range ('September 2-11'), expand it to every date in the range.

deliver.shape: JSON array, one object per RFC example, exactly the fields below

fields.name: n
fields.rule: example number in RFC order

fields.name: description
fields.rule: the RFC's line, word for word

fields.name: dtstart
fields.rule: the RFC's DTSTART line

fields.name: rrule
fields.rule: the RFC's RRULE line, or '' for RDATE-only examples

fields.name: extra
fields.rule: RDATE/EXDATE lines, or ''

fields.name: occurrences
fields.rule: ISO local datetimes

fields.name: truncated
fields.rule: true when only the first 20 are given

self_check: Every row has a URL you opened yourself today, on the maker's, agency's or store's own site (never a blog, forum, wiki, reseller, or AI summary).
Every quote is copied word for word from that page or PDF page and is there now.
Every number has its unit in its own field; no number is estimated unless the field says 'math' and shows the arithmetic.
No row is a copy of another with the names changed.
The file is valid JSON (or exactly the code/markdown asked for) and is named exactly as asked.

checks: Claude runs every example through an independent recurrence library and through Kairos's ics.js; any disagreement with the RFC is a defect in the file.
